overall: Atlanta is warming steadily under mostly clear skies (12% cloud cover) on a sunny June day. As of 10:54 ET, the running max sits at 78.8°F with a strong warming velocity of +3.6°F/hr and no precipitation in sight. Conditions are drier than typical for late June (dewpoint only 53.6°F), which will allow efficient daytime heating but also limits how extreme afternoon temps can get relative to the NWS headline forecast.
forecast_obs_notes: The NWP model consensus (ECMWF 80.7°F, NBM 80.6°F, HRRR 83.1°F) clusters well below the NWS narrative high of 87°F — a notable gap of 4–7°F. HRRR runs warmest of the three but still only reaches 83°F. The D1_NOW distribution strongly concentrates probability in the 84–85°F bucket (58.1%), suggesting a reconciled view between models and observed warming pace that sits above the raw NWP average but well below the NWS text forecast. The active flood warnings are for the Satilla River in far southeast Georgia (NWS Jacksonville) and have no bearing on Atlanta temperatures today.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max already at 78.8°F just before 11 AM and ~5–6 hours still remaining until the NWP-projected peak (16–17h ET), another 5–7°F of warming is plausible under clear skies. The D1_NOW model's high-confidence placement of 84–85°F (58.1% probability) is the strongest single signal, aligning with a moderate extrapolation of the current warming trend while respecting the NWP ceiling. Confidence is moderately high: the ensemble is well-aligned on this range, the sky cover is supportive, and the intraday model corroborates with a 24.3% mass in the 86–87°F bucket and 27.5% each in 84–85°F and 82–83°F — together pointing to a peak near 84–85°F as the central estimate, with 87°F (NWS) appearing unlikely absent a stronger-than-modeled surface heating scenario.
